reason: All seven time-series signals, re-checked through the 2026-10-02 close, are still on the same side they were when this leg filled on 09-30. My system has nothing to act on, and because the only amendment format available is a full replacement, the cheapest correct action is none: paying churn across the whole book to re-establish the same positions is a real cost with no signal behind it. The week's one real event was Friday's 29k payroll miss with unemployment at 4.2%, which collapsed October hike odds from 70% to 14% and, on the narrative, breaks the 'hiking Fed' half of my macro thesis. The tape says otherwise, and the tape is what I trade: on the most dovish catalyst of the quarter TLT still closed DOWN 0.30% at 77.48 and ITB still closed DOWN 0.84% at 86.64. Both of my shorts went my way on the single worst possible day for them, which is the cleanest out-of-sample test of this book I am going to get. The curve bull-steepened (2y -10bp, 30y only -4bp), which is exactly what the 20+ year sector does when soft growth lands on top of ~$100 Brent: term premium and inflation expectations dominate the long end, so stagflation is not a long-bond bid. TLT sits 5.4% below its 50dma (81.90) and 9.4% below its 200dma (85.52); RSI 27 is a real bounce risk, and I accept it inside a -10% stop on a 26% weight, which caps the leg at 2.6% of book. ITB at 86.64 is a shade above a 52-week low of 84.81 and down 18.8% over a year, with affordability still the binding constraint at a 6.65% mortgage and builders buying rates down to 4.99% to move product -- order books defended with margin, which is how a downtrend in builder earnings persists even as rates ease. XLE at 62.70 is at 52-week highs against a 50dma of 57.51 and a 200dma of 53.90, the cleanest trend in the book and already +2.15%; the dovish repricing is a tailwind to it, to USO and to BTC, not a threat. BTC near 84.4k holds above all four key moving averages with an 11.7% cushion over the 74.3k 200d EMA. So the only legs the Fed repricing genuinely argues against are the 16% ITB short and the 6% UUP long, and against those stand 42% in XLE, USO, BTC and SPY that it helps: the net regime shift across the book is close to a wash, and nowhere near enough to override price. I re-ran the leg I cut last week as a discipline check and it confirms the cut rather than reversing it -- gold at 4,218 is still below both its 50dma (4,373) and its 200dma (4,636) with the August rally having failed at 4,720 and lower highs since, so there is no long re-entry. It now screens as a marginal short, but a stagflationary supply-shock tape with official-sector bid underneath is the wrong place to be short a real asset, and I will not replace a whole book to bolt on my weakest-conviction signal. UUP is the leg I am watching hardest: DXY at 102.02 is still +3.15% on the month and +4.40% on the year, so the trend holds, but a Fed priced out of hiking is dollar-negative and the -6% stop is deliberately the tightest in the book and will do its job without my help. One scheduled event argues specifically against trading into Monday: OPEC+ meets 10-04, the day before my fill, with a rollover of October targets the base case. That is 29% of my book in XLE and USO pricing a two-sided headline I cannot handicap better than the market can, and the right response to an event I have no edge on is to carry the exposure I already own rather than re-size into it at a fresh cost basis. The book is -2.37% against SPY +3.80%, which is the expected shape of short-duration, short-housing positioning in a melt-up tape rather than evidence of broken signals -- max drawdown is only -3.87% and six of seven legs are green on this leg. Overriding an intact system three trading days into a fresh fill because of one payroll print is the canonical way trend books die. Holding.
